objective: Review the RescueStock technical design, revision 1 (submission sub-mv1c60sc-01174690, spec.md sha256 ea9c0c68c84ee761210a4271b4a5148a90623c54a085dab8281b3e73d4595b2c), against the approved architecture brief (sub-mv1awqkf-017ea892, approved by rev-mv1bcexb-01d7960e) and its 45 required criteria, and check that the five open minors ARCH-22..26 are resolved.
context: The spec has the six required headings (Components, Interface Contracts, Data Design, Security, Testing Strategy, Deployment). It also covers Technology Choices, Background Processing (payment saga, void rule, reconciler, supersession), AI / LLM Design (wire schema, local validator, prompt, CLI and API adapters, fake, EXT-1 eval plan with thresholds), Frontend, Observability, Performance, Recovery, Implementation Workflow, Open Questions and a Criterion Traceability table (45 ids to design section and test file). The first table maps ARCH-22..26 to their resolutions. Decisions used: dec-mv16pyxx-01bad0bf, dec-mv16pz0g-01d5c4c2, dec-mv16pz32-013c4cd1. Memory search returned one toolkit-guard lesson (mem-sd-mv1audrd-013b7102), not applicable to the product, so it was not cited. External facts are listed with source and date: the PayPal claims stay 'verify' because the primary docs are blocked here; the Anthropic structured-output field was taken from the primary docs page on 2026-10-09; the CLI flag constraints were verified locally.
inputs: examples/groundwork/src (adapter, auth and db patterns, read only)
expectedOutput: A recorded review of design submission sub-mv1c60sc-01174690 covering the 45 required criteria and ARCH-22..26.
acceptanceCriteria: gate show design lists the same 45 required ids (RS-01..RS-39, NFR1..NFR6)

ARCH-22: the void rule sets cancel_requested_at on every non-terminal operation; any transition into authorized with cancel_requested_at set queues exactly one void (so:<id>:void:1); [D] test void-rule-lost-authorize; row-2 escalation clause

ARCH-23: the claim uses the stored authorization_expires_at (no provider call before or inside the claim); the provider re-read happens after the claim, by the lease holder, with AUTHORIZATION_EXPIRED compensation; RS-20 wording unchanged

ARCH-24: node-proc helper passes the allow-listed execArgv and merges --experimental-sqlite into NODE_OPTIONS on Node < 22.13; the 22.5 pass condition includes RS-14, RS-20, RS-26 and lease-takeover (ev:ev-mv1bgxsc-010de90b)
ARCH-25: auth routes, cookie, TTL, rotation, provisioning, admin password, SQLite sign-in throttle with a [D] assertion, webhook route CSRF-exempt and signature-only

ARCH-26: PayPal timeout 20 s against a 60 s lease (config refuses lease < 3 x timeout); takeover increments lease_epoch and resolves every capture call in intent/unknown by reading provider state before any send; writes fenced on executor_id + lease_epoch (+ lease_until > now for call starts) and on a per-call send_token; lease-takeover test variants A/B assert exactly one capture per order
Interface contracts are exact enough to build both sides: method, path, request/response types, error codes from the one catalog, auth role, idempotency rules, limits
Data design: every table with types, constraints and indexes; append-only triggers on inventory_ledger and audit_events; numbered migrations 001-005
completedWork: Read the approved brief in full, plus goal.md, the research notes, the review findings and the recorded decisions. Ran two probes as evidence. ev:ev-mv1bgxsc-010de90b: node --test forwards execArgv to test files, grandchildren need NODE_OPTIONS or explicit execArgv, and the host presets NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192, so the helper merges. ev:ev-mv1bh8wb-011b5cf0: the CLI's stream-json input requires stream-json output and --verbose. Checked the Anthropic structured-output docs (output_config.format, no beta header, supported schema subset). Wrote .eccode/artifacts/design/spec.md and submitted it. Key decisions: (1) a provider-call protocol (queue/start/record with send_token fencing, stale-intent rule of 2 x timeout, read-before-resend table per call kind); (2) a plan lease_epoch fence; (3) the post-claim authorization read; (4) ARCH-22 resolution hook; (5) supersession never triggered by other customers' reservations, so RS-14's loser gets OUT_OF_STOCK; (6) dedupe of webhooks only among valid signatures; (7) a provider-safe wire schema plus a stricter local validator with grounding checks; (8) node:test plus the Playwright library for test:browser (global install or devDependency); (9) seeded and self-registered accounts, admin from RS_ADMIN_PASSWORD.
remainingIssues: OQ-D1: design-level reasons beyond the brief's trigger lists (executing -> non_executable AUTHORIZATION_EXPIRED from ARCH-23; approved -> non_executable OUT_OF_STOCK; REQUEST_DELETED, DEMO_RESET; supersede reasons REPLANNED, AVAILABILITY_DROPPED). Default: adopt.
OQ-D2: the brief's derivation has no row for an executed plan after an admin post-execution refund. Default: P executed and any op refunded -> cancelled.
OQ-D4: Anthropic model id claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 and the prices are configurable and marked verify.

OQ-D5: PayPal facts to confirm on the first Sandbox run (approval link rel, authorization statuses incl. EXPIRED, final_capture rejecting a second capture, PayPal-Request-Id replay and retention, capture/refund ids via GET order, webhook event names).
The CLI stream-json stdin/result shapes for image input are verified only at the first live-model run (cli-image-smoke); until then a recorded transcript is used.
Carried from the brief: Q1-Q8, Q9 (Node floor; both branches designed), Q10 (daily model budget USD 1.00).
nextAction: technical-reviewer: review design submission sub-mv1c60sc-01174690 with eccode gate review design, covering the 45 required criteria and ARCH-22..26.
